Each handoff makes the child one generation deeper, so the chain was always going to terminate; nothing in the skill, the generator or the health checker knows the ceiling exists. ⚠ CORRECTED THE SAME HOUR, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF. CYC-0020 first recorded this as BLOCKING, on the reasoning that AUT-PROP-019/020 need a reviewer who did not author the text and no session could be created. ⛔ THAT WAS WRONG, AND research-loop §3 SAYS SO IN PLAIN TEXT: the blind seats of a hardening round are PARALLEL SUBAGENTS, not spawned sessions. A subagent starts with a fresh context and has never seen the authoring, which is exactly what 'blind' means here. The seats ran as five concurrent subagents at the governed width. ★ THE LESSON IS NOT ABOUT THIS CEILING: an agent that cannot use its FIRST choice of mechanism must enumerate the others before calling work blocked, and 'blocked' is a claim that needs evidence (CLAUDE.md §0). CYC-0020 also ran only ONE cycle of its permitted two, so it never owed a handoff at all. ⛔ THE LIVE RISK IS NARROW AND REAL: a session that REACHES its 2-cycle cap while at depth 8 cannot comply with §3, and `health.py`'s `cycles_are_sized` reads `handoff.child_session_id` — so it would score that session RED for failing to do something the platform forbids. ⭐ WHAT TO FIX: teach the handoff path to detect the refusal and fall back to the driver Routine explicitly (record that the Routine carries the next cycle, rather than leaving the field absent), and teach `cycles_are_sized` that a depth-refused handoff with a live driver Routine is GREEN. ⚠ A cycle may NOT fix this by disabling or re-arming the driver Routine — §7 forbids acting on a `created_via: http_api` Routine from outside it, and `fire_trigger` refuses it too.
